transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time to meet. As you know, next Thursday we're conducting a student-family reunification exercise following a simulated building evacuation, and I need to approve the final operating plan before the exercise notice goes out to families. The draft currently uses the gymnasium as the reunification site, one transportation wave, an on-site medication table, and English-only pickup forms. Before I sign off, I'd like to hear from each of you — the school nurse, facilities coordinator, transportation coordinator, and family liaison — so we can identify any concerns or gaps. Let's start with the nurse: does the on-site medication table setup work for your needs?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a transportation issue with the draft plan. I confirmed this week that the exercise group includes 96 students, but the school has only one available 50-seat bus because the second bus is assigned to another school. Transportation policy therefore requires exactly two bus waves — not one, as the draft currently assumes.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a language-access gap in the draft plan. My family contact review, completed this week, shows that Spanish and Somali are the two additional languages needed for pickup instructions. The plan must provide pickup forms in English, Spanish, and Somali, and have an interpreter available. These language-access details have not yet been entered in the draft.

transcript.text: The on-site medication table setup does not work for my needs. My current health-plan list identifies four students whose emergency medications must remain in temperature-controlled storage, and the nurse's office refrigerator is the only approved storage location during the exercise. I confirmed this storage requirement while reviewing the health plans this week, but the draft plan still lists an on-site medication table. We need to revise the medication plan to account for temperature-controlled storage at the nurse's office rather than a table at the reunification site.

I confirmed this week that the gymnasium floor will be sealed and inaccessible next Thursday from 7:00 a.m. through the end of the exercise. The cafeteria is the approved alternate reunification site. I received the facilities work-order confirmation, but the gym closure has not yet been added to the exercise plan, so the draft still lists the gymnasium as the reunification site.

transcript.text: Thank you, everyone, for flagging those concerns. To summarize what I'm hearing: Nurse Okafor needs temperature-controlled medication storage at the nurse's office instead of the on-site table; Mr. Bell has a facilities conflict requiring us to move from the gymnasium to the cafeteria; Ms. Hart has identified that we need two bus waves rather than one for 96 students; and I've flagged that pickup forms must be provided in English, Spanish, and Somali with an interpreter available. Dr. Vega, it sounds like the draft plan needs revisions in all four areas before it can be approved. I'd suggest we update the draft to reflect these changes and circulate it for final review before the notice goes to families.
